newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Market premature on Westpac-BML deal-ACCC.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Market premature on Westpac-BML deal-ACCC.

text.p: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) Chairman Alan Fels said on Friday that the market assessment on the merger between Westpac Banking Corp and Bank of Melbourne was premature.
Westpac shares rose sharply on Thursday and Bank of Melbourne shares fell as speculation grew that the ACCC would not approve the merger.
"This was a very strange reaction. It was just some rumour that got right out of hand," Fels told reporters.
He stressed that he did not mean the market had got it wrong, merely that they had pre-empted the ACCC deliberations.
Fels said the anti-monopolies authority's probe on the merger was focused on transaction accounts and the ACCC did not have concerns about the implications of the merger on the home loan market.
"I guess also in housing loans, except that we know that a competitive market and we don't have any concerns there," Fels said,

He said the ACCC's delay in making a decision on the merger also was partly due to ongoing inquiries into how Westpac aims to ensure some form of automony and separate for the Bank of Melbourne post-merger.

"We would also be looking at credit cards and we'll also be having a look at the role of the bank of melbourne in small business dealings, even though it does not have a very big role at the moment," he said.
Westpac shares were two cents firmer at A$7.22 at 10.25 a.m. (0025 GMT), after having risen 25 cents on Thursday.
Bank of Melbourne shares were 15 cents firmer on Friday morning, after having dropped 39 cents on Thursday.
